examples.title: A constructed standards body: where the critical mass falls
examples.label: constructed, not observed: proved laws in counts, without noise, read on people by an AI reading; its test, CMT, frozen 5 November 2026 and not run; no test has human participants
examples.markdown:
*Constructed, not observed. The numbers are illustrative. The laws are proved in counts, without noise ([02 §9](chapters/02-MAP.md#r-shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected)); reading them on a body of people is an AI reading.*

A standards body of 30 members decides each round which practice its rule favours. Some members are *shapers*: they back a new shared format and carry the capacity to shape the rule; the others keep the status quo. That the rule's readers are drawn from the members it selects, and that each new seat carries the practice of the one it replaces, are the model's premises, not facts about any body.

Take `a = 1`, `p = 0`, `c = 3`, `hi = 7`, `lo = 1`: each shaper among the readers reads 7 coming back to the shapers, each other reads 1, and backing the format costs 3. The rule read favours the shapers (weakly) exactly where `x.carrier · c + x.other · c ≤ x.carrier · hi + x.other · lo`, whatever `a` and `p`; with `lo ≤ c ≤ hi`, exactly where the shapers stand to the others at least as `c − lo` to `hi − c`. Here that is 2 to 4, the shapers' share `(c − lo)/(hi − lo)` = 1/3 ([record](results/records/shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected.md#correspondence--对应)): 10 of 30.

- 12 shapers: 90 against 84 + 18 = 102. Strictly favoured, their share rises strictly at every step, every configuration locked.
- 8 shapers: 90 against 56 + 22 = 78. Strictly disfavoured, it falls strictly at every step.
- 10 shapers: 90 against 90, a tie; the share stays.
- A cost of 2 puts the mass at 1 to 5, 5 of 30. Adding `p` to every member moves it nowhere.

**What it predicts, and how far.** Without noise the start decides. Drawn one member at a time, neither lock holds for good: either is left by drift, at a weight whose bound shrinks across the distance from the mass, and which state one member arising fixes more often depends on `a` and `p` as well as `hi`, `lo` and `c` ([drawn one at a time](chapters/02-MAP.md#r-drawn-shaping-drawn-one-at-a-time)). At an even count the shapers are risk dominant exactly where `2c < hi + lo` (6 < 8 here), and risk dominance can part from which state fixes more often.

**Its test.** [CMT](../../experiments/critical-mass-located/DESIGN.md) would read this location on people's groups in published laboratory stag hunts whose payoffs the experimenter set, screened before any choice is seen. It was frozen on 5 November 2026 and has not run; a pass would bound the mass on the side of one half only. No test of the account has had human participants ([what is empirical](COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md#5-what-is-empirical)). Nothing here ranks a course: that needs C or a premise in its place.

examples.title: Two courses for a valley: T8 under its two premises
examples.label: constructed, not observed: a use of an argued thesis (T8) under two unasserted premises, beside a proved law of widening (any type, finite listing)
examples.markdown:
*Constructed, not observed. T8 is argued, not proved; its two premises are stated, not asserted.*

A valley weighs three courses. Course A keeps the river's fishery, its wetland and the village school, and adds a clinic. Course B keeps the same, with no clinic. Course D adds a factory and new trades, and ends the wetland and the reed-cutters' way of life, which A keeps.

**What needs no premise.** A *widens* B: at every step it admits all that B admits, and at some step more. Proved for any type on a finite listing: one course widens another exactly when every positive weighting ranks it higher, and a mixed comparison is decided both ways ([07 §4.4](chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#r-widening-as-what-every-positive-weighting-ranks)). A and D are mixed: each admits something the other does not.

**What the two premises add** ([07 §4](chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#scope-and-order)). The *continuation condition* fixes scope, whose losses count: every continuation's, the reed-cutters' and the wetland's among them; its step of invariance extends scope to losses that return to no one. It ranks nothing. *C*, widening what can form is better, gives order: it ranks A above B. Neither is asserted. C leaves A against D unranked: an expansion that ends forms of life another course keeps both exceeds that course and fails to include it, so the two are mixed ([07 §9](chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#objections)). Choosing between them takes further premises, each named: a reading of `living`, the lifting L and the commitments J1–J4 ([07 §5](chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#practical-judgment)).

**T8** reads this as the way for life: 生生, life in the whole and its continuing generation [AI reading], compared by widening, scope from the condition and order from C ([07 §8](chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#theses)). *For life* says whose way it is, not whose losses count. Its standing is argued; open are P2 and P4 with P3, the step of invariance and a reason for C; no verdict binding every possible mind is claimed. It falls to a mixed case argued better from every standpoint counting everything positively, with no further premise, or a pure closing argued good for life.

**What it does not show.** Whether anyone in the valley fares better: 07 shows no well-being beyond admitted continuation, no value of bringing new lives into existence, and no duty, right, recognition, motivation or compliance ([07](chapters/07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#does-not-show)). 生生 is not any new organization, nor the map's generation, which allows loss ([glossary](../../GLOSSARY.md)). The five earlier folders chapter 5 lists as applications elsewhere, community and cooperative designs among them, are design programmes, not results; correspondence not established ([05 §11](chapters/05-COLLECTIVES.md#joint-plans), [the earlier folders](../README.md)).

open_doubts:
What I read: ONE-PAGE.md in full; GLOSSARY.md in full; theories/README.md in full (it is the atlas-generated folder table); COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md in full (it is at theories/becoming/COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md); 05-COLLECTIVES.md §1 (all of it), §11, §12, "What this chapter does not show" and "Open"; 02-MAP.md §9's opening paragraph, the RuleShaping, DrawnShaping, drawn-one-at-a-time and read-in-time theorems, T7 and the two Readings after it, and "Which locks noise leaves"; the record shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected.md, its Correspondence and Dependencies only; CMT's DESIGN.md §0 to §5, §7, §10 to §13 and §15 (not §6's verdict rule, §8, §9's dry-run tables or §14), and REVIEW-FREEZE.md round 1 only; 07-SIGNIFICANCE.md §4's head and table, §4.4's opening theorem and the self-concern theorem, §5's head, the ranking table and the four-responses conditional, §8 (T4, T5, T8), §9, "does not show" and "Open"; OPENING.md's "This is a foundation" paragraph, its notes [^alignment] and [^guardian], and its header; the overview's §5 and part of §7. I did not read the DrawnShaping Lean module.

Symbols. The brief names `s` among the drawn-shaping model's parameters. DrawnShaping has no `s`: `s` is RuleShaping's (what comes back to the shapers alone), and DrawnShaping puts `hi` (read by shapers) and `lo` (read by others) in its place. DrawnReplacement also uses `s` as a count ("the rule read at `s`"). So the example uses `a`, `p`, `c`, `hi`, `lo`, `x.carrier`, `x.other`. The share `(c − lo)/(hi − lo)` is not in 02's theorem text, which gives the ratio `c − lo` to `hi − c` (`critical_iff`). The share appears in the record's Correspondence (an AI reading), in the module docstring as CMT quotes it, and in experiments/README.md. The example cites the record for it.

Anchors. The stag-hunt Reading ("without noise the start decides"; "nothing here ranks a course") has no anchor of its own. It sits after T7 under `#t7`, so I cite it as 02-MAP.md#t7. The COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION and CMT anchors assume GitHub-style heading slugs (#5-what-is-empirical, #6-what-enough-situationality-would-have-to-mean, #the-answer-in-brief, #what-is-frozen-and-what-it-can-refute). I did not check them against the renderer. theories/README.md links 05 as #11-joint-plans-and-applications; I used the explicit anchor #joint-plans instead.

Where the homes differ in wording or could pull apart:
(1) ONE-PAGE says the commons law is "Proved on models; restates the commons". 05 says "restates the tragedy of the commons and overshoot ... in near-definitional arithmetic, not who ought to take less". These are consistent; I quoted both.
(2) COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION says "no test has human participants". CMT, if run, would read existing laboratory data from human groups. That would be human data, not participants recruited by the account. The line is true while CMT is not run, but it may need rewording once CMT runs.
(3) CMT's freeze record has a sixth round with one medium finding, and on 5 November a seventh round was approved, on that change's diff. experiments/README.md says simply "frozen 5 Nov 2026, not run". I did not check whether the seventh round finished before FROZEN.sha256 was committed.
(4) The opening's coordination sentence is in the first person ("I hold that this foundation supplies that too"). I restated only its thesis clause, impersonally. The OPENING header says that sentence is "now held in the first person".

Naming. CMT's design names specific AI model pins as possible coders, and it names the person whose call the run is. The drafted text names neither. It says only "has not run".

Mapping. 07 never uses the phrase "human development". Mapping the row to T8 and to 07's "does not show" list is the page's framing, not a home's. The valley and the standards body are constructed. Calling the standards body's members "shapers" and "readers drawn from the selected" is my AI reading, labelled as such in the example.
